name: FM synthesis carrier/modulator/ratio basics
goal: Explain and patch basic FM: carrier vs modulator operators, amplitude→modulation depth, frequency→rate, stacking modulators (including slow modulators for evolving vibrato), audio-rate FM for bright spectra, self-mod, and preferring simple frequency ratios (1:1, 2:1) for musical results vs inharmonic mess.
prerequisites: FM-capable synth or Web Audio FM (at least 2 operators)
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided captions; do not invent UI or settings.
Original synthesis only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Pigments/Phase Plant/etc.) to portable osc/filter/FX roles for a browser or generic hybrid synth; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable signal-flow and motion relationships over vendor-specific preset names.
Educational FM procedure only — map to whatever operator UI the host provides.

steps.action: Start with a sine carrier; confirm frequency→pitch and amplitude→loudness.
Add a very slow sine modulator into carrier frequency at low depth — hear vibrato-like pitch wobble; raise modulator amplitude to deepen FM.
Raise modulator frequency into audio range (and/or change modulator shape, e.g. saw) to create bright/complex spectra (laser-like extremes possible).
Optionally modulate the modulator with a slower operator for evolving vibrato/depth; try self-mod carefully.
Name parts: operators; algorithm = routing graph; modulator vs carrier roles; set ratios near simple integers (1×, 2×) for musicality; avoid unrelated ratios when you need tonal results.

verification: Simple ratio sounds more tonal than arbitrary ratio at same depth
